items.title: Add stable validation command identity and a normalized command-set digest
items.context: Plan sections 'Stable command identity' and Story 1 exit. ValidationCommand (packages/main/src/core/validation-types.ts) has label/command/args/cwd/env/optional/timeoutMs/resources but no id. Add an optional declared `id`, a deterministic provisional id derived from the normalized executable tuple for legacy commands, duplicate-id rejection, and a commandSetDigest over the normalized inventory. Identity must never be inferred from array index, and existing `focus` tags must be kept for compatibility but excluded from relevance computation.
items.userSees: Running `node packages/main/dist/tasks/validation-tier-planner-smoke.js` prints a line per identity case and ends with `validation-tier-planner-smoke: PASS`. Running `proof-or-stop validation_plan --storyId=B-a745 --tier=fast` on this repository lists every configured command with an `id=` value, and each id for an entry that declares none is prefixed `prov-` to mark it provisional.

happy.desc: A configured command that declares an id keeps exactly that id; a command that declares none receives a deterministic provisional id derived from the narrow portable tuple of command, args, repo-relative resolved cwd and shell.

verification.selector: declared id is preserved verbatim and is not marked provisional

happy.desc: The same command set produces the same commandSetDigest across two independent computations, and changing any normalized field of any command changes that digest.

verification.selector: commandSetDigest is identical across two independent computations

edge.desc: Two configured commands whose narrow normalized tuples are identical are rejected as a duplicate id error naming both entries, rather than silently coexisting or being deduplicated.

verification.selector: two identical narrow tuples are rejected as duplicates naming both entries

edge.desc: Moving a command to a different array position does not change its provisional id; identity is never derived from index.

verification.selector: moving a command to another array position does not change its provisional id

edge.desc: Renaming ONLY a command's label leaves that command's stable id unchanged AND changes the commandSetDigest, because the spec requires a label rename to invalidate the selection command-set digest while the id survives for graph continuity.

verification.selector: renaming ONLY a label keeps the stable id and changes the commandSetDigest

edge.desc: While any command in the inventory still relies on a provisional id, a migration warning is emitted naming how many commands still lack a declared id; once every command declares one, the warning is absent.

verification.selector: a migration warning names the runtime count of commands still lacking a declared id

adversarial.desc: Adding the optional id field to ValidationCommand leaves the existing routine validation identity digest byte-identical for a command set that declares no id, while actually declaring an id in the project config does change source.inputDigest, proving the new identity can only add refusal conditions and never remove one.

verification.selector: the optional id leaves the routine identity digest byte-identical, while declaring it in config changes source.inputDigest

verificationEvidence.note: The fixture asserts a declared id survives verbatim; the companion prov- case in the same run covers the undeclared half.

Resolve a checklist verification-evidence pin to exactly one command id: exact commandId match first, else normalize the legacy free-form command string with the SAME executable/argv normalization the routine identity uses and compare the complete normalized tuple (command, args, resolved cwd, shell, relevant environment). Exactly one match records pinResolution=legacy-exact plus the normalized-tuple digest; zero matches stop with pinned_command_missing; more than one stops with pinned_command_ambiguous. Labels and array order must never break a tie, and historical evidence is never rewritten in place.
items.userSees: The smoke run prints one line per pin case and ends `validation-tier-planner-smoke: PASS`. On a story whose verification evidence pins a command string that no longer matches any configured command, `proof-or-stop validation_plan --storyId=B-xxxx --tier=fast` stops and prints `pinned_command_missing`, naming the unresolved pin; when the string matches more than one command it stops and prints `pinned_command_ambiguous`, naming every candidate id.

happy.desc: Evidence carrying an explicit commandId that exists in the current universe resolves to that command and records pinResolution=exact.

verification.selector: an exact commandId match resolves and is recorded as a declared-id resolution

happy.desc: Legacy evidence carrying only a free-form command string that normalizes to exactly one configured command resolves to it and records pinResolution=legacy-exact plus the normalized-tuple digest.

verification.selector: a legacy string matching exactly one command records legacy-exact and the normalized-tuple digest

edge.desc: A legacy pin string that normalizes to no configured command stops with pinned_command_missing and produces no plan.

verification.selector: a legacy string matching nothing stops as pinned_command_missing with no plan

edge.desc: Commands differing only by resolved cwd, or only by shell versus argv form, are treated as distinct by the resolver and do not collide.

verification.selector: commands differing only by resolved cwd are distinct

adversarial.desc: A legacy pin string that normalizes to two or more configured commands stops with pinned_command_ambiguous, and neither a differing label nor array order is allowed to break the tie; the resolver must not return a first match.

verification.selector: two commands with identical normalized tuples stop as pinned_command_ambiguous listing every candidate

verificationEvidence.note: Exact commandId resolution path.

verificationEvidence.note: SUPERSEDED INTENT, not an unmet one. This intent reads: 'A legacy pin string that normalizes to no configured command stops with pinned_command_missing and produces no plan.' That behaviour was DELIBERATELY REVERSED during REVIEW by the fix for finding B-a745:F-001, so no honest mechanical evidence for it can exist -- the stated behaviour is gone by design. Under the new behaviour an explicit commandId that does not resolve STILL stops with pinned_command_missing, while a legacy free-form string that normalizes to nothing is classified pinned_command_non_inventory, escalates to repository-full, and does not stop. WHY THE CHANGE WAS MADE: the old behaviour made the command self-referentially unusable (evidence for the planner pinned the planner, so the planner stopped BECAUSE evidence existed for it) and would have stopped on essentially every real story, since verification evidence pins test binaries that are not validation commands. Fail-closed is preserved: nothing is ever pruned, and repository-full is the same width the stop would have widened to. WHO VALIDATED IT: the decision was escalated to the main agent by the implementer rather than improvised, the reasoning was independently checked and endorsed by the proof-or-stop-review-behavior lane (pass RP-002), and the governing spec was found to contradict ITSELF on this point -- its widening matrix says only an EXPLICIT pin stops, its resolver step 4 says any no-match stops. That contradiction is filed for the spec owner (story B-ccf4) to reconcile. WHAT IS ACTUALLY COVERED BY COMMITTED FIXTURES, in place of this intent: 'an unknown commandId stops as pinned_command_missing and produces no binding' (the surviving stop path), 'a legacy string matching nothing is a non-inventory evidence command, not a stop' and 'a non-inventory legacy pin plans repository-full instead of stopping, and seeds no command' (the replacement behaviour, both branches). The test-coverage lane verified both branches are covered (pass RP-004). This waiver records that the acceptance criterion moved under review, with reviewer sign-off; it does not excuse an untested behaviour.

items.title: Add the Story input collector producing a normalized StoryRelevanceInput
items.context: Plan section 'Story input contract'. Collect Story identity/phase, base/HEAD/material/story-files hashes, rename-aware changed paths via changedFilesBetweenRenameAware or changedFileStatusesBetweenRenameAware (packages/main/src/core/evidence-freshness.ts), checklist files.modify/create/test and evidence command pins (see packages/main/src/handlers/delivery-context-pack.ts for existing collection semantics), risk signals, and the routine source kind plus execution inventory. Deleted files and both sides of a rename stay seeds; Story metadata and registered runtime artifacts are not material seeds; a failure to read the changed-file set must escalate rather than read as 'no changes'.
items.userSees: The smoke run prints one line per collector case and ends `validation-tier-planner-smoke: PASS`. `proof-or-stop validation_plan --storyId=B-a745 --tier=fast --explain` prints a `Story inputs` block listing the rename-aware changed material paths, the checklist-declared modify/create/test files, the resolved evidence pins, the risk signals, and the routine source kind, and prints an `unclassifiedInputs` list that is empty when every seed was classified.

happy.desc: For a story with committed changes the collector returns rename-aware changed material paths, checklist files.modify/create/test, resolved evidence pins, risk signals, and the routine source kind, each seed carrying its provenance.

verification.selector: the collector gathers every Story input kind with per-seed provenance

happy.desc: The collector reads changed paths through the existing evidence-freshness rename-aware reader rather than shelling out to its own git invocation.

verification.selector: the collector defaults to the SHARED rename-aware reader and the shared hash snapshot

happy.desc: The collector gathers command duration history from prior signed validation artifacts and reports commands with no recorded history as unknown-duration rather than as zero.

verification.selector: duration history is collected and an absent history reports unknown-duration, never zero

happy.desc: The collector carries verification intent through as human-readable reason context available to the explain output.

verification.selector: verification intent is carried as reason context and produces no command-to-seed edge

edge.desc: A deleted file remains a seed, and a renamed file contributes both its old and its new path as seeds.

verification.selector: a deleted path remains a seed and a rename contributes both old and new paths

edge.desc: Story metadata paths and registered runtime artifacts are excluded from material seeds by the same canonical classifier used for material freshness, not by a local path list.

verification.selector: story metadata and registered runtime artifacts are excluded by the canonical classifier

adversarial.desc: When the changed-file read fails, the collector reports changed_files_unavailable and an escalation rather than returning an empty seed set that would read as no changes.

verification.selector: a changed-file read failure is changed_files_unavailable, never an empty seed set

adversarial.desc: Duration history is estimate-only and verification intent is reason-context-only: a fixture mutates duration history and asserts the selected set is unchanged, and a fixture asserts verification intent alone produces no command-to-seed edge.

verification.selector: mutating duration history leaves the selected set and the selection digest unchanged

verificationEvidence.note: All input kinds collected with per-seed provenance.

items.title: Add language-neutral planner types and the fail-closed widening matrix
items.context: Plan sections 'Terminology and invariants', 'Selection algorithm' steps 1, 2 and 5, and 'Fail-closed widening matrix'. Define the tier names story-fast / story-intermediate / repository-full, the subset invariant, the reason-code enum from the matrix, and the resolver that maps a StoryRelevanceInput plus a requested tier to an effective tier with escalation reasons. In this Story the resolver ALWAYS returns effective repository-full or a classified stop; it performs no pruning and an empty selection is never a PASS. Source kinds fallback / validate-file stay atomic and no-validator preserves the existing skip/warn.
items.userSees: The smoke run prints one line per planner case and ends `validation-tier-planner-smoke: PASS`. Every `validation_plan` invocation prints `requestedTier:` and `effectiveTier:` on separate lines, and in this Story `effectiveTier` is always `repository-full` or the run stops; it is never `story-fast` or `story-intermediate`. Each escalation reason prints as `<reason_code> - <one sentence in plain language>`.

items.title: Add the read-only validation_plan CLI with --explain and --json
items.context: Plan section 'Proposed CLI and UX'. Register `proof-or-stop validation_plan --storyId=B-xxxx --tier=fast|intermediate|full` with --explain and --json in the command catalog. Output must show requested and effective tier, selected versus full count derived at runtime, inclusion reasons grouped by command, unclassified inputs, escalation reason codes, estimated duration and basis, whether the run is final authority (fast/intermediate: no), and the artifact path/digest when one is written. The command writes no evidence, executes no validation command, and changes no gate. Note the plan's `--focus` / `--tier` mutual-rejection rule applies to the future `validate --tier` command in Rollout Story 4, not to `validation_plan`; do NOT implement that rejection here.
items.userSees: `proof-or-stop validation_plan --storyId=B-a745 --tier=fast` prints `requestedTier: story-fast`, `effectiveTier: repository-full`, `selected: <n> of <n> commands`, a `finalAuthority: no` line, the inclusion reasons grouped per command, the unclassified inputs, and each escalation reason with its plain-language gloss. Adding `--json` prints the same facts as a single JSON object. `proof-or-stop validation_plan --tier=fast` with no storyId exits with `validation_plan: storyId is required`.
